stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and null spec. Live Preview of Content in CMS across GO, UP, MX platforms is complex — involves real-time rendering, cross-platform behavior, and potential security concerns with preview content. openspec runs first to elaborate AC and technical depth; speckit follows to harden testability, edge cases, and security around preview rendering.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story — Contentstack Live Preview SDK integration. No existing live-preview mechanism in the codebase; useContent (236+ callers) is the attachment point. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so all criteria assume a mocked Live Preview client and assert observable behavior at our boundary.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with valuable context: useContent is the attachment point (236+ callers), Contentstack is unreachable at test time, and all criteria should assert observable behavior at our boundary. I built the full AC list from scratch based on the story title and openspec's notes. Key design decisions: (1) AC-3 ensures no performance/behavior regression when preview is off — critical for production. (2) AC-4/AC-5 cover connection lifecycle (loss + reconnection) since Live Preview depends on a persistent connection. (3) AC-6 covers malformed data since Contentstack preview payloads may diverge from published schema. (4) AC-7 addresses XSS since CMS content is user-authored. (5) AC-8 addresses credential exposure since Live Preview SDK requires configuration. (6) AC-9 covers accessibility for dynamic content updates per WCAG 4.1.3. (7) AC-11 prevents over-rendering since useContent has 236+ consumers. (8) AC-12 prevents blocking initial render on slow SDK init. All ACs are observable outcomes with no implementation instructions. I could not review the actual useContent implementation or Contentstack SDK docs, which would have allowed more precise boundary assertions — this is flagged below.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: OpenSpec provided valuable context (useContent as attachment point, Contentstack unreachable at test time, mocked client recommendation) but failed its primary deliverable — it produced zero acceptance criteria (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0). Speckit compensated by authoring the entire AC set from scratch based on the title and OpenSpec's notes. The resulting 12 ACs are well-conceived (performance regression, connection lifecycle, malformed data, XSS, credential exposure, accessibility, over-rendering, non-blocking render), but the collaborative pipeline did not function as designed — Speckit should have been hardening OpenSpec's ACs, not creating them wholesale. Additionally, Speckit flagged it could not review the actual useContent implementation or Contentstack SDK docs, which limits the precision of boundary assertions. A human should verify the ACs against real implementation constraints before approval.
